Using toil

What every toil command shares, in detail - the envelope and errors, the contract version, --select, toil wait, paging and progress, writes and their exceptions, global flags, files and the workspace, configuration, the raw API passthrough, dossiers, the audit log, using toil from a program (@imagile-dev/toil/api), certificates and proxies

Docs / Using toil

SKILL.md has the rules every call needs. This page has the detail behind them, for when a call needs more than a command’s own flags.

The envelope and errors

Every command prints one JSON envelope on stdout: { ok, data, error, meta }. Check ok; on failure, error.code says what kind of failure it was and error.fix says what to do about it. New codes may appear in any release, so treat a code you don’t know as a generic failure. meta.warnings lists anything worth knowing that isn’t a failure, such as a truncated result. meta.context says which connection a call used and how it was chosen, and where any project, repo or environment it resolved came from. --pretty formats the output for people.

meta.contractVersion (also in toil version) is the version of toil’s command contract: its commands, flags, data fields, envelope and error codes. It goes up only with a breaking change, so a script or program built against one version works with every toil that reports it.

Paging

Paged results put the next page’s cursor in meta.page.nextCursor (null on the last page) and the page size in meta.page.limit. Pass the cursor back with the command’s own paging flag, which its reference names.

Progress

While a command runs, toil says what it’s doing: each page a listing reads, and each rate-limited (429) request it waits to retry. On the command line these go to stderr, one plain [toil] … line each: a retry and how long toil waits always, piped or not, and pages only when stderr is a terminal. stdout still holds only the envelope. Over MCP they’re progress notifications, sent when the client’s call asks for progress. A program using toil’s API gets them, and every request too, through onProgress (Using toil from a program). They never change the envelope.

Selecting fields

To get back only the fields you need, pass --select <expression> (select over MCP), a JMESPath expression applied to data, for example --select "issues[].{key: key, status: fields.status.name}". meta, including meta.page, is left as it is. A bad expression is INVALID_INPUT before the command runs, with its position in error.fix; one that selects nothing gives data: null and a SELECT_EMPTY warning.

Waiting for something to finish

To wait for a build, a scan or a deployment to finish, don’t call a read in a loop: toil wait --until "<expression>" -- <read command> runs it again every --interval (default 15s, at least 5s) until the JMESPath expression over its data is true (not null, false or empty), for example toil wait --until "result != null" -- jenkins pipeline get-run --name my-job --number 42 or toil wait --until "projectStatus.status != 'NONE'" --timeout 10m -- sonar quality-gate --project my-app. Over MCP it’s the wait tool, with tool (the read’s tool name), input (that tool’s input) and the same until, interval and timeout. It returns the read’s last envelope plus meta.wait (until, attempts, elapsedMs). NETWORK errors and HTTP 5xx or 429 answers are retried with backoff; any other error ends the wait with that error. Past --timeout (at least 5s; default 30m, or TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS, cut to the maximum with a WAIT_TIMEOUT_CAPPED warning when it is longer; at most the "wait": { "maxTimeout" } in config, default 1h) it’s TIMEOUT, with the last data in error.details.data. Only reads can be waited on: a write is INVALID_INPUT. --select before wait applies to the final data; a --select after -- belongs to the read, so --until sees what it selected. Other global flags go before wait.

Writes

Reads are always allowed. A command that changes something, in a service, a database or a file on this machine outside toil’s own config, needs both writes: true on the connection it uses, set by a person in their config or with a TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_WRITES / TOIL_<AREA>_WRITES env var, and --allow-write on the call (allowWrite: true over MCP). Without either it fails with WRITE_DISABLED, naming what’s missing. Over MCP a write tool isn’t listed until writes are on, and deletes are never tools. A command that is CLI only and has no connection yet (toil skills marketplace add) needs --allow-write alone.

Exceptions

Exactly three writes don’t follow that rule. Each is the maintainer’s choice, made deliberately, and is listed here with how to avoid it.

WriteWhat it writes, and whenWhyTo avoid it
toil skill installWith --allow-write alone (CLI only, no connection): the toil skill, into one agent’s skills folder as toil/, recorded as bundled.Its contents are fixed: the files embedded in toil, no third-party code. It replaces only a toil/ folder it recorded as bundled and refuses any other.Don’t run it.
The toil skill keeping itself currentWith no --allow-write: a toil/ skill folder recorded as bundled, and nothing else in a skills folder (never a marketplace or hand-made skill). Rewritten by any command that loads config, on the CLI or over MCP, when that command changed the config file (a connection added, changed or removed) or when the copy was written by another toil version. Said in meta.warnings as SKILL_REWRITTEN.So an installed skill never describes connections you no longer have, or a toil you no longer run, with no update command to forget. The contents are fixed; the description holds only area and engine names checked against toil’s own list, never a host or a credential; and a rewrite that fails is a SKILL_REWRITE_FAILED warning, never a failed command.Don’t install the skill with toil skill install (copy skills/toil yourself, or use the Claude Code plugin marketplace), or delete the installed toil/ folder. A call with --config <file> never rewrites it.
The welcome menu’s game saveWith no --allow-write: the game’s progress, under the "game" key of ~/.toil/config.json, every other key kept as it was. Only while you play Two Weeks’ Notice in the menu bare toil opens.It’s a game a person plays at a terminal, and its save touches nothing but its own key. The save is sealed against tampering, not kept secret.Don’t play it. There is no setting to turn the save off.

The raw API passthrough

For an endpoint no command covers, an HTTP area has toil <area> api <METHOD> <path> (<area>_api over MCP), which sends the connection’s own credential to a path under its base URL. GET and HEAD are reads; other methods are writes, and DELETE is CLI only. The area’s reference describes it where the area has one (jira.md).

Files and the workspace

Files a command reads or writes (an --input-file, an upload, a download, a CSV report) must be inside the workspace: --workspace <dir>, else TOIL_WORKSPACE, else the working directory; under toil mcp, the client’s root when it shares exactly one. Relative paths resolve against it, a path outside is refused with INVALID_INPUT, and nothing is ever overwritten. Under toil mcp with no single root, a command that touches a file returns NOT_CONFIGURED: add --workspace <dir> to the server’s args. A person can let commands reach any path with "bounds": { "files": "unbounded" } in their config, and every envelope then carries a BOUND_RELAXED warning. Saved paths come back absolute, with forward slashes. Commands that run git need git on PATH and say GIT_NOT_FOUND without it; nothing else does.

Configuration

Configuration comes from environment variables, which always win, or from ~/.toil/config.json (or the file passed with --config). A connection is one instance of an area; --connection <name> picks one when there are several. toil connections list names them (never a secret), and toil connections test <name> checks one with a single authenticated read, failing with the AUTH, NETWORK or config error a real command would. Setting up a connection, signing in, turning writes on and choosing a default are for a person: a bare toil in a terminal opens a menu for them.

Global flags

Global flags go before or after the command: --pretty, --verbose (adds every request to meta.requests, credentials redacted), --debug (traces on stderr), --config <file>, --output-file <file> and --workspace <dir>. --help on any command lists its own flags.

Dossiers

A dossier holds what toil knows about one body of work: its repositories, and per area the keys a call needs (project, owner, a namespace per environment), which connection to use (by name, or by host), and reference data such as board lists. It holds no secret and can’t add a host or turn on writes. toil reads dossiers on every area command from ~/.toil/dossiers/, the folders in dossierPaths (or TOIL_DOSSIER_PATHS), and .toil/dossiers/ in the repository you’re in, and uses the one that applies: --dossier <name|file> (dossier over MCP, or TOIL_DOSSIER), else the one whose repo matches the folder by path or origin remote. --cwd <dir> (cwd over MCP) looks from another folder. A value you pass always beats the dossier’s, and meta.context.dossier says which dossier applied and why. When two different dossiers match, the call fails with INVALID_INPUT until you pick one. A write on a connection a dossier chose is WRITE_DISABLED unless the dossier is in your own folder; pass --connection to choose it yourself. To see what a call will use before making it: toil dossiers context (which dossier a folder resolves to and why), toil dossiers show [name] (per area: the connection and why, whether writes are on, the environment and the inputs), toil dossiers list, and toil dossiers check [name], which checks one locally and contacts no service.

To build one for a product: toil repos scan lists the git repositories under the workspace. Then:

  • toil dossiers init <name> creates the dossier.
  • toil dossiers add-repo <name> <folder|remote> adds each repository.
  • toil dossiers link <name> <area> --host <host> --set project=PAY [--for-repo <repo>] says which connection an area uses and the keys it supplies.
  • toil dossiers env <name> <env> <area> --set namespace=... adds an environment.
  • toil dossiers field <name> jira storyPoints customfield_10002 names a field, so --field storyPoints=5 works.
  • toil <area> check-dossier checks a section against the service, for the call’s environment (jira, jira-cloud, confluence, sonar, ado, bitbucket, github, openshift, dynatrace).
  • toil dossiers export <name> --repo <root> writes a shareable copy into a repository’s .toil/dossiers/. It uses host selectors and no local paths, and toil never commits it.
  • toil dossiers unlink <name> --area <area> [--env <env>] removes a section (CLI only).
  • toil dossiers import <file> copies a teammate’s into your own folder. A connection or host you lack is listed under toSetUp; toil never creates one.

These are local writes and need no --allow-write. Each refuses a value that’s already set unless --replace. Over MCP they refuse to make a dossier select a connection with writes on; the user does that on the command line, or under Dossiers in the menu bare toil opens, which runs these same commands and asks them to type the connection’s name first.

The audit log

toil keeps a local audit log of every command it runs, through the CLI, MCP and the API: one JSON line per call in ~/.toil/audit/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl, with the command, front door (via: cli, mcp or api, plus caller when a program named itself), connection, whether it wrote, the outcome, the redacted input and each request’s method, URL and status. It never holds a secret, a header, a body or a row, and db SQL is kept only as a SHA-256 hash. toil audit list reads it back, newest first, with --since <date>, --command <name|area>, --connection <name> and --writes-only; toil audit path says where it is and whether it’s on. Six months are kept by default ("audit": { "keepMonths": 12 } changes that), and only a person can turn it off, with "audit": { "enabled": false } in ~/.toil/config.json. A call whose line couldn’t be written still succeeds, with an AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED warning.

Using toil from a program

A Node program can call toil in-process instead of running toil and parsing stdout. @imagile-dev/toil/api is a supported entry point of the same package, with its own types, and it adds no dependency: it is the same bundle as the CLI. Loading it runs nothing, even when your own build bundles it in: only toil’s bin starts the CLI.

import { contractVersion, execute, registry, version } from '@imagile-dev/toil/api';

if (contractVersion !== 1) throw new Error(`Needs toil's contract 1; toil ${version} has ${contractVersion}.`);
const envelope = await execute('jira search', { jql: 'project = PAY', maxResults: 50 }, {
  readOnly: true,
  caller: 'nightly-sync',
  onProgress: (event) => console.error(event.message),
});
  • execute(command, input, options) runs one command and returns its envelope, exactly as the CLI prints it. command is the name meta.command reports (jira search); input is the command’s MCP fields, checked strictly. It never throws: an unknown command or a bad option is an INVALID_INPUT envelope. Connections, env vars, the credential store, dossiers, the workspace (the program’s working directory, else workspace), the write gate and the audit log all apply as they do on the CLI. It serves what MCP serves: commands that prompt or change connections, and deletes, stay on the CLI.
  • options: readOnly refuses, with WRITE_DISABLED and before anything is sent, any call that would change anything, whatever the config says: a write to a service, and a local one too (toil’s config or dossiers, a download, a file named with out). A read-only call writes nothing but its audit line. caller names the program in the audit log (lowercase letters, digits, ., _ and -, up to 64). signal cancels the call (CANCELLED). onProgress hears every request (redacted URL, status, time), page and retry. config, workspace and verbose match --config, --workspace and --verbose.
  • registry lists the areas and every command execute() serves: its name, MCP tool name, whether it writes to a service (writes) or on this machine (writesLocal), and its input’s JSON Schema.
  • version and contractVersion are what toil version reports. Check contractVersion before relying on anything else. toil version also reports commit, the 40-character hash of the commit the build came from (null when the build didn’t record one), which is what a bug report from a terminal names.
  • mapOwi(input, options) maps envelopes you already hold (one, an array, or JSON Lines text) to Open Work Items, the way toil util owi map does (util.md), synchronously and without the schema check: { items, histories, skipped, warnings }. options.fields is a dossier section’s fields object ({ estimate: 'customfield_10234', estimateUnit: 'points' }), command names the command for bare data, and key the item a keyless history belongs to. A refused input throws, with a fix. owiVersion is the OWI version items carry, and owiSchema their JSON Schema; execute('util owi map', { text }) maps and validates in one call.

What @imagile-dev/toil/api exports, and the types it names, follow the command contract: they change only additively unless contractVersion goes up. Anything else in the package is internal.

Certificates and proxies

toil trusts the OS certificate store and Node’s bundled CAs, and uses HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY when they’re set. A NETWORK error about an untrusted certificate means the CA is in neither; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS adds it.
